meaning_by_symbol.LEAK: dark corners, fading edges, perimeter dim, thin hum
meaning_by_symbol.THERM: hot and dim, rumble, rough, reddish
meaning_by_symbol.STALL: frozen and dim, silent, cold, unresponsive
meaning_by_symbol.RESON: one face blazing and vibrating, whine, others normal
meaning_by_symbol.DRIFT: sliding light, blurred edges, wavering pitch
meaning_by_symbol.ECHO: too bright, layered hum, frozen patterns
meaning_by_symbol.LOWIN: all dim, whisper hum, washed out
meaning_by_symbol.HIGHIN: blazing all faces, harsh buzz, heat
meaning_by_symbol.PHASE: opposite faces pulse bright and dark, two-tone hum
meaning_by_symbol.DEADLK: one or two corners glowing, clicking, heat at corners
meaning_by_symbol.BSOFT: wobbly edges, bulging faces, muffled hum
meaning_by_symbol.CVOID: normal glow, hollow tap, dark center, surface hum
meaning_by_symbol.UNK:: the following brief description is a new or unknown symptom that does not match any existing code
meaning_by_symbol.FAIL: the previous step for the referenced code failed, so retry with more detail rather than re-diagnosing
meaning_by_symbol.done: the instructed action has been executed and completed

reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry paradigm survives the evidence requirements. The suggested suffix family -FT is unsupported: DRIFT and BSOFT do share final letters, but their initial residues do not form a coherent substitution class in a stable shared frame, and no consistent compositional contribution for FT is recoverable. The suggested suffix family -IN is also insufficient: LOWIN and HIGHIN contrast in overall intensity, but the rest of each meaning bundle is not predictably derivable from a shared suffix plus substituting stems, so this does not meet the compositional predictability requirement. Other recurrent substrings (e.g. LOW/HIGH, SOFT, SPLIT, VOID, etc.) likewise lack minimal-pair evidence in a common frame. The control/status items UNK:, FAIL, and done are also best treated as opaque lexical symbols rather than segmented morphology. Therefore the safest analysis is a flat lexicon.
